title: Why Is My HVAC Filter Wet?
h1: Why Is My HVAC Filter Wet, and What Should I Do?
description: A wet HVAC filter usually means a clogged condensate drain, a frozen coil that thawed or a filter placed too close to the coil. Here is how to find the cause.
quick_answer: A wet HVAC filter usually means water is backing up or dripping where it shouldn't. The most common causes are a clogged condensate drain line, an overflowing drain pan, an AC coil that froze and then thawed, or a filter installed too close to the coil. High humidity and a leaking high-efficiency furnace can also be to blame.
body:
Your air conditioner pulls moisture out of the air as it cools. That water drips off the indoor coil into a drain pan and flows out through a condensate line. A filter should stay dry through all of that. When it's damp or soaked, something in the system isn't draining or flowing the way it should.

What causes a wet HVAC filter?

  • A clogged condensate drain. Algae, sludge and dust build up in the drain line. When it clogs, water backs up into the pan and can overflow onto nearby parts, including the filter.
  • A cracked or rusted drain pan. Older pans can crack or rust through and leak.
  • A frozen coil that thawed. Low airflow or low refrigerant can freeze the coil. When it thaws, more water than usual drips and can soak the filter.
  • A filter too close to the coil. In some setups, the filter sits right next to the coil and catches drips or condensation.
  • A high-efficiency furnace leak. These furnaces produce their own condensate. A loose or clogged furnace drain can leak near the filter.
  • High humidity. In damp coastal weather, cold surfaces around a filter rack in an attic or garage can collect condensation.
  • A leaking duct or roof. Less often, rainwater from a roof leak or a condensing duct in the attic can drip onto a ceiling filter grille.

Why is a wet filter a problem?

A soaked filter restricts airflow, and that can make the coil freeze, which makes the problem worse. A damp filter is also an easy place for mold to grow, and that mold gets blown through the house. If water is overflowing, it can damage drywall, ceilings, flooring and the equipment itself. In attic systems, an overflow can show up as a stain on the ceiling below.

What should I do right away?

  1. Turn the system off at the thermostat.
  2. Remove the wet filter and replace it with a dry one.
  3. Look for water around the indoor unit, drain pan and nearby ceiling.
  4. Check for ice on the coil or the larger copper line. If you see ice, leave the system off for cooling and let it thaw, or run the fan only.
  5. Look for the condensate line outlet outside. If it isn't dripping while the AC runs, the line may be clogged.
  6. Check the float switch. Many systems have a safety switch that shuts off the AC when the pan fills. If the AC won't run, that may be why.

Can I clear the condensate drain myself?

Some homeowners clear a simple clog by using a wet/dry vacuum on the outside end of the drain line. Many lines also have an access port near the indoor unit where a technician pours a cleaning solution. If you're not sure where the line runs, or the unit is in a hard-to-reach attic, have a technician handle it.

If the coil froze, find out why before running the AC again. A dirty filter is the simple answer. Low refrigerant means a leak, and that's not a DIY repair.

How do I keep my filter from getting wet again?

  • Have the condensate drain cleared during your yearly AC tune-up.
  • Change the filter on schedule so airflow stays strong.
  • Keep supply vents open to prevent coil freezing.
  • Ask about a float switch if your system doesn't have one.
  • Have the filter location checked if it sits right next to the coil.

When should I call a technician?

Call if the filter keeps getting wet, if you see water stains on the ceiling, if the coil keeps freezing, or if the system shuts off on its float switch. A technician can clear the drain, check the pan and coil and find whether airflow or refrigerant is behind the problem.

faqs: Can a wet filter cause mold?
Yes. A damp filter gives mold a place to grow, and the system can spread spores through the house. Replace a wet filter right away and fix the source of the water before putting in a new one.
Why is my AC filter wet only in summer?
That's when the AC makes the most condensate. A partly clogged drain line or an overflowing pan may handle light use but back up during long, hot days. Clearing the line usually solves it.
Is it safe to run my AC with a wet filter?
It's best not to. A wet filter restricts airflow, which can freeze the coil and make leaks worse. Turn the system off, swap in a dry filter and find out why it got wet.

A float switch is a small safety device in the drain pan or drain line. When water rises too high, it shuts off the AC to prevent an overflow. If your AC suddenly won't run and the pan is full, the switch may have tripped.
